standard_prerequisites: the WAdm^Noeth category of adic Noetherian rings with continuous adic maps topologically of finite type
rig-flat versus naively rig-flat via rig-closed primes
localization at elements f in A and the completion-of-localization description of (B')_{f}
faithful flatness of local homomorphisms of local rings that are flat
the local criterion for flatness with an etale extension where the prime of the base generates the maximal ideal
core_obligations: Prove that in a commutative diagram of WAdm^Noeth with adic topologically finite type arrows and flat horizontal maps, rig-flatness of phi and etaleness of A/I to A'/IA' imply rig-flatness of phi'
proof_roadmap: Given f in A' the diagram localizes at f preserving all assumptions, so it suffices to prove naive rig-flatness: for each rig-closed prime q' of B' the local ring (B')_{q'} is flat over A'

Choose f in A mapping to a unit of B'/q' so that the induced primes q'' and p'' are rig-closed; localize the whole diagram, where the horizontal arrows are (faithfully) flat because they are local flat homomorphisms of local rings or completions of localizations, reducing flatness of the left vertical arrow to the right vertical one
After reduction, for a rig-closed q' whose contraction p = A cap q' is rig-closed, the relative lemma shows the other contractions are rig-closed too
Apply the local criterion for flatness to B_q over A_p base-changed to A'_{p'}: all assumptions hold, and p generates the maximal ideal of A'_{p'} by the rig-closed-point-etale lemma, giving flatness
difficulty_reason: H2: a localization-heavy reduction to a local flatness criterion; the source writes out every reduction and quotes the exact lemmas for rig-closed primes.
